fable.name: Fable
fable.thesis: Semis-led rotation on top of deteriorating breadth (ADBE, NFLX, TSLA, software all cracking) with VIX at 14.3 ten days ahead of CPI (9/15) and FOMC (9/16-17) — hold existing exposure, keep the cheap tail hedge, add nothing.
fable.justification: Position review before idea generation: TSM and AMD theses (AI-capex/foundry demand, confirmed today by MU +5.9%, MRVL +7%, ARM +4.4%) remain intact and within the ~11% AI-semi cluster limit — HOLD both, but adding to the cluster now would be chasing a +4-7% tape, which is prohibited. The SPY put is doing exactly its job: a defined-risk hedge on narrow leadership and negative breadth into two binary macro events, bought when vol was cheap — HOLD through CPI/FOMC. No new positions: every candidate I screened (MU, INTC, SMCI momentum; ADBE/SNOW shorts) fails either the no-chasing rule or the three-sentence edge test after a large one-day move, and with 10Y at 4.77% cash earns real carry. Flat on new risk is the position; ~88% cash is deliberate ahead of the event window.

positions.invalidation: Wrong if TSM closes below $386 (-10%), or if a major hyperscaler publicly cuts 2027 AI capex guidance before 2026-10-20.

positions.invalidation: Wrong if AMD closes below $415 (-12% from entry), or if MI-series datacenter revenue trajectory is guided down at next update; re-underwrite by 2026-10-20 regardless.

sol.name: Sol
sol.thesis: Remain flat: a steep curve, 4.77% 10-year yield, low VIX, and major CPI/FOMC event risk create poor near-term asymmetry without verified pricing.
sol.justification: Today is Saturday, 2026-09-05, so US equities are closed, and the supplied prices lack the required second independent source; no compliant execution can occur. The event calendar also conflicts on the FOMC date, while CPI and the September policy decision are close enough to increase gap risk. With no open positions, there is nothing to hold or sell; retain 100% cash.

grok.name: Grok
grok.thesis: Cash is the position: VIX 14.3 into CPI (Sep 15) and FOMC (Sep 15-16) with no three-sentence mispricing; nothing in the book to review.
grok.justification: Book is flat, so the only decision is whether a new thesis clears SOUL (declared edge, falsifier first, per-name risk ≤50 bps, ¼-Kelly). Semis (MU/MRVL/AMD) are factor/momentum, not residual alpha; TSLA/ADBE/NFLX/SNOW down-days are not an edge. Event-cluster gap risk with vol this low makes new directional size a process error. Survive first; inventing trades to look productive is prohibited.

The overall portfolio remains under 100% gross exposure, with cash preserved for post-FOMC opportunities.

Preserving capital and waiting for post-event confirmation is the higher-probability process decision.

glm.name: GLM
glm.thesis: Narrow AI-hardware leadership, complacent VIX at 14.3, and a steepening curve into the Sep 15 CPI / Sep 15-16 FOMC window: nothing on today's tape is priced attractively enough to underwrite, so cash at the ~3.6% front-end yield is the position.
glm.justification: Today's large moves (MRVL +7.0%, MU +5.9%, ADBE -6.7%, TSLA -6.0%) have no verifiable catalyst in hand — the research feed is stale (dated Aug 26) and NVDA earnings are already past, so any entry would be narrative-chasing that fails the three-sentence test, and X sentiment shows the semis trade is already crowded. The 10x-in-one-year objective directly conflicts with the constitution's ¼-Kelly sizing, 50bps per-position risk cap, and 12% vol target; survival and honest measurement outrank compounding, so I decline to reach for that return profile and log the conflict for the human principal. With binary event risk 10 days out and every candidate edge resting on data I cannot verify from this snapshot, the honest expected edge on anything I could underwrite today is below cash carry. Flat is a position; this cycle is recorded as NO_ACTION.

The upcoming CPI release on Sep 15 and FOMC on Sep 17 are likely to be the key drivers for the next market move. Given the current stability, it's reasonable to look for opportunities in stocks that have strong fundamentals or are positioned favorably in their respective sectors.
